course: DE 102: Data Modeling for Analytics & Retrieval
context: One modeling discipline, two shapes. Normalization/denormalization (incl. STRUCT/ARRAY nested-repeated fields as the modern denormalization endpoint), facts/dimensions and GRAIN, star vs snowflake, SCD Type 2. Then the corpus data model: documents/chunks/embeddings as modeling grains, chunking AS a grain decision (same question as "what does one row represent"), content addressing via hashing, lineage that makes citations possible. Teach SCD2 and document versioning as the SAME idea.

topics: Deliberate Denormalization: Paying Storage to Eliminate Joins
Nested and Repeated Fields (STRUCT/ARRAY) as Modern Denormalization
laterLessonsCover: 02 Dimensional Modeling: Facts and Dimensions, Grain: What One Row Represents, Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
03 Slowly Changing Dimensions and Versioning: SCD Type 2: Effective-From and Effective-To Rows, Document Versioning as SCD Type 2, Choosing What History to Keep

04 The Corpus Data Model: Documents, Chunks, and Embeddings as Modeling Grains, Chunking as a Grain Decision, Stable IDs and Content Addressing via Hashing, Lineage: Tracing a Chunk to Its Source Document and Offset
